subject: Transportation Systems
title: Radar at Sea
description: A fast breakdown of Radar at Sea for builders.

hook.text: At night or in fog, a ship's officer can't see other vessels. Radar shows them all on a screen.

buildup.text: Marine radar sends out radio pulses that bounce off ships, coastlines, and buoys.

discovery.text: The returning echoes paint a picture of everything within 20 to 50 miles of the ship.

twist.text: Radar can't detect small wooden boats or objects sitting low in the water. Limitations persist.

climax.text: Modern ARPA radar tracks targets and calculates collision risk automatically.

punchline.text: Radar lets ships see in the dark.

quiz.question: What is a limitation of marine radar?
options: It can miss small wooden boats or low objects
